title: Kansas City nightlife and jam sessions; Prez blows Budd Johnson out of the hall
summary: In Kansas City they went everywhere, jamming at the Subway; Budd Johnson, the local modern tenor king, cried when Prez came in and out-played him.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: He didn't go too many places. The only place he liked to go out was when he was playing there. He wouldn't go out to a show or nothin' too much. Not like we did, you know. In Kansas City we'd go everywhere. Go to all the nightclubs. amd

down to where there was jammin'... See, in Kansas City in them days, they had about ten or fifteen or twenty places where they'd go and jam. Les, he jammed in a place called the Subway. They went down in the Subway... Everybody come by there in the a.m., all the horns, through the night. See, this guy hired him... When the Blue Devils band was there and they were laying off, well, he would go down to the Subway and work, make four or five hours. That's about all in them days you'd make, you know...
Who'all did you hear jammin' in Kansas City? Any kind of interesting jam sessions you might have heard back then?
Oh yeah. A lot of them. Budd Johnson. Yeah, Budd Johnson cried when Prez walked into Kansas City.
Well, Prez blew him out the hall. See, Budd had been the king around there on the tenor -- in the modern style of tenor. There were a lot of tenor players around there.
